outcome: Non-study antibiotic use in the facility prior to delivery
Non-study antibiotic use after delivery until facility discharge
Non-study antibiotic use after discharge to 42 days post-partum
cohort: The study included 29,278 pregnant women enrolled in the A-PLUS trial across eight Global Network sites in seven low- and middle-income countries.
finding: Non-study antibiotics were frequently used among pregnant women, with 17.1% receiving them prior to delivery, 40.8% after delivery until facility discharge, and 47.6% after discharge up to 42 days postpartum, primarily for prophylaxis, though use varied substantially by site and time-period.
country: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
